themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Surge in Sunset Park
themes_detail.summary: Nine dead or dying tree complaints filed THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks (650% spike, z-score 5.97)—a dramatic environmental deterioration signal that coincides with illegal tree damage complaints also spiking 454% last week (9 complaints vs. 1.6 avg), suggesting possible contractor negligence, disease outbreak, or infrastructure damage.
evidence: 9 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score 5.97)
9 illegal tree damage complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (454% spike, z-score 5.24)
Combined 18 tree-related complaints in past 2 weeks suggests systemic issue, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Investigate whether a single contractor or city agency is responsible for tree removal or pruning; cross-check DOB permits for tree work
Consult arborists: are trees dying from disease, pest infestation, or infrastructure work (water mains, sidewalk repair)?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Explodes in Sunset Park
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 5 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week (1900% spike, z-score 10.97, highest z-score in dataset)—the most statistically extreme anomaly in the entire district, signaling a potentially new or emerging open-air market or distribution hotspot requiring immediate investigation.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1900% spike, z-score 10.97—highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Spike is recent and concentrated, not diffuse across 90-day period, suggesting new or accelerating problem
No corresponding Reddit discussions or local news mentions suggest story is not yet covered
reporting_angles: Map the 5 complaints geographically: are they clustered in one park, intersection, or transit node? Interview NYPD and local precinct about enforcement strategy.
Interview residents and street outreach workers about visibility of drug use; check whether this coincides with known fentanyl or synthetic opioid distribution patterns in Brooklyn

themes_detail.label: Boiler Failures Spike This Week
themes_detail.summary: Three boiler complaints filed THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.5 per week (500% spike, z-score 5.0)—a sudden surge in heating system failures during winter season that directly impacts tenant habitability and may signal a broader building code enforcement gap or aging infrastructure crisis.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 5.0)
Heat/hot water complaints represent second-highest complaint category overall (1,064 over 90 days), indicating chronic baseline issue now accelerating
Timing in winter season amplifies urgency: tenant habitability violations under NYC Housing Maintenance Code §27-2029
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 3 boiler complaints with DOB violation records and Housing Court cases to identify which buildings are repeat offenders
Interview tenants in affected buildings about lack of heat; contact DHCR (Division of Housing and Community Renewal) about enforcement actions

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Accelerates
themes_detail.summary: Eighteen sidewalk condition complaints filed 3 WEEKS AGO (the most recent comparable data point) versus a baseline of 5.9 per week (206% spike, z-score 4.19)—a sustained street infrastructure problem that aligns with the community board's recurring request for street upgrades and suggests unmet maintenance backlog.
evidence: 18 sidewalk condition complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 5.9 weekly average (206% spike, z-score 4.19)
Street Condition complaints also in top 10 (449 total over 90 days), indicating pervasive pavement issues
Community Board's recurring budget request for street upgrades suggests this is a known, unresolved problem
reporting_angles: Request DOT data on sidewalk repair backlog and budget allocation to CD 307; compare to other Brooklyn districts
Document specific hazardous sidewalk locations with photos; interview residents about trip/fall incidents

themes_detail.label: General 311 Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Twelve 'General' category complaints filed THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 5.4 per week (123% spike, z-score 4.01)—an undefined complaint surge that signals either a frustrated resident population reporting miscellaneous grievances or a data quality issue, warranting spot-checking of actual complaint content.
evidence: 12 'General' category 311 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly average (123% spike, z-score 4.01)
'General' category lacks specificity; spike may indicate residents using catch-all category due to frustration or system confusion
Coincides with multiple other spikes this week (dead trees, boilers, drug activity), suggesting possible district-wide distress signal
reporting_angles: Request sample of the 12 'General' complaints to identify actual underlying issues; interview 311 operators about call patterns
Monitor whether this is a temporary reporting anomaly or evidence of broader resident dissatisfaction
